status: corrected and locked for Phase 04 abstract implementation
scope: abstract protocol, activation, compromise, and fault semantics; no cryptographic implementation

B1.name: Triple-KEM/PQNoise-style SDLS key update
source_supported_semantics: the construction is a standalone key exchange that outputs fresh SDLS key material
final keys are derived only after the handshake is complete for the party in question
missing or out-of-order required fragments cause abort/drop unless another layer repairs ordering or loss

primary_confirm_loss.meaning: ground completes and activates locally after sending KEM_CONFIRM; spacecraft remains on the previous epoch when the message is lost

enhanced_policy.name: DEFER_UNTIL_AUTHENTICATED_STATUS
enhanced_policy.purpose: measure an explicit four-message operational integration rather than use hidden simulator knowledge

status_loss.meaning: spacecraft activates when sending authenticated status; ground remains on the previous epoch if status is lost

non_attribution: Neither activation policy is specified by the Triple-KEM paper.
The paper does not specify an operational SDLS commit, rollback, or installation-acknowledgment procedure.
The enhanced status-gated variant adds a fourth message and does not solve the last-message problem by itself.

B2.name: Poettering-Roesler URKE-inspired strict evolution baseline
B2.construction_family: unidirectional ratcheted key exchange using generic KEM encapsulation and evolving endpoint state

strict_model_decisions.sender_transition: ground derives the new session state and deletes the prior sender state when the update is sent
strict_model_decisions.receiver_transition: spacecraft derives and installs the matching state only after accepting the update ciphertext
strict_model_decisions.status_telemetry: evidence of completion, not a ratchet transition

TRAFFIC_KEY.future_key: a fresh legitimate update replaces the exposed key

passive_interval.future_key: secret if copied sender state is not used to desynchronize the receiver

RECEIVER_STATE.future_key: traceable for the receiver and corresponding in-sync sender

non_attribution: This is a TT&C operational adaptation of the URKE state-evolution pattern, not a conformance claim.
The simulator does not implement the paper's cryptographic algorithms or inherit its proof.
Strict deletion and lockout classification are experimental operational choices.

requirements_before_T1: corrected B1 activation policies encoded in tests
B2 traffic-key and state-exposure scopes encoded separately
baseline fault outcomes stable under deterministic replay
independent cryptography review of the semantic mapping
